exposure: vaginal misoprostol (25 mcg every four hours)
outcome: neonatal complications (e.g., NICU admissions, lower Apgar scores)
cohort: 106 pregnant women at term undergoing induction of labor.
finding: Both misoprostol and Dinoprostone are effective for labor induction, but misoprostol shortens the induction-to-delivery interval while increasing cesarean rates and fetal complications, whereas Dinoprostone shows better fetal outcomes and fewer complications despite a longer induction-to-delivery interval.
mod_finding: Dinoprostone resulted in higher vaginal delivery rates (73.58%) and fewer cesarean sections compared to misoprostol (50.94% vaginal delivery).
